newsitem.title: FRANCE: France's Chirac pledges work to end child abuse.
newsitem.headline: France's Chirac pledges work to end child abuse.

text.p: French President Jacques Chirac, speaking 13 days before a parliamentary election, pledged on Monday to work to stamp out child sex abuse and protect the young from threats ranging from drugs to religious sects.
Chirac, a conservative, said he was revolted by a spate of sexual attacks in France.

"I am determined to do everything to fight against this depravity of our society and to punish those who carry out these abject acts," he said on the steps of the Elysee Palace after talks with a group representing family associations (UNAF).
He said both the authorities and families had responsibility to "protect children from everthing that threatens them in society -- delinquency, violence, drugs, but also sects".
The head of UNAF, Hubert Brin, said he was counting on Chirac to help families whoever won the May 25-June 1 parliamentary election.
Opinion polls show Chirac's centre-right allies are likely to retain power. Chirac plans to serve the remaining five years of his seven-year term even if the opposition Socialists win.
France has also been shocked by Belgium's paedophilia scandal of kidnap and murder and less publicised cases of rapes and killings of children in France.
Last week, a former teacher from Cosne-sur-Loire was detained and placed under investigation on suspicion of a spate of abuse. About 60 people have filed suits against him.

Two brothers are being probed on suspicion of raping and killing four student girls near Boulougne, northern France in February. Last year, a 13-year-old British schoolgirl was raped and strangled in a youth hostel in Brittany.
